what_it_does: When chip designers want to speed up a specific piece of software, they often build a custom hardware block (an accelerator) for it. Traditionally, a human engineer picks which part of the program to accelerate and manually writes a hardware description. Cayman automates this: it reads the program, identifies which sections (kernels) are worth turning into hardware, and generates an accelerator design automatically. It also optimizes how the main processor hands data to the accelerator and takes results back, and it finds opportunities to merge multiple accelerators into one reusable block — reducing chip area. The approach handles programs with complex branching logic (control flow), not just simple loops, which most prior tools cannot.
